summary: All four T3 tile mini-scenes are built and verified, with a preview at a stride, the loop seam (or the end frame for the non-looping toy town), a 200 px readability row, meta with measured final s/f, and a hex contact sheet each. Continued from an interrupted builder; finished scenes were not restarted. t_jelly_cubes (60-f seamless loop) was verified as is: the preview matches the current script and the seam is pixel-identical. Its final cost was measured. t_duck_pool (90-f loop): two stale preview frames (f30, f60) were re-rendered, the seam was checked and the final cost measured. t_sunset_bunny (180-f loop): the gold showed olive-khaki patches where it reflected the HDRI's cool sky (G2 muddy). These became warm amber via a glossy-rays-only rose tint on the map. The preview stride and every seam frame 172-181 were re-rendered and the cost re-measured. t_toy_town is NEW: a candy town on a lavender cake-plate on a sky cove. The sun sweeps one day over 180 straight frames (loop null). Long morning shadows point right, swing round behind the houses at noon and stretch left in the evening. Cool lavender sky fill colours the shadows, and the windows glow at dusk. Total final cost for the four scenes is about 0.29 GPU-h. Every scene is under the 0.12 GPU-h cap, measured on an idle GPU 6.

deviations: t_toy_town is 180 straight frames, not a loop (meta loop null). The spec allows '180 frames at 30 fps', and a morning -> evening day cannot loop without rewinding the sun.
t_toy_town: the sun power follows ~1/sin(elevation)^0.6, which is non-physical. A real low sun lights the ground 4x weaker and the long shadows drowned in the sky fill.
t_toy_town: solar time is warped, s = t - 0.45 sin(2 pi t)/(2 pi), so the long-shadow ends linger and noon passes 1.45x faster.
t_toy_town: the cove carries a faint self-lift in its own sky colour (emission strength 0.22, emission sampling NONE) so the backdrop never goes grey-lavender when the sun is low.
t_toy_town: motion blur is off because nothing moves geometrically.

t_sunset_bunny: reflection (glossy) rays see the sunset map through a rose tint #FFCFD8. Camera rays see the pastel coral BG, and diffuse rays see the untinted map. A sun lamp locked to the map's sunset azimuth adds the shadows (it sits at 22 deg elevation vs the map's 4.5 deg glow).
t_sunset_bunny: the bunny scan is Laplacian-smoothed (volume-preserving) for a cast-gold finish (predecessor's choice).

t_duck_pool (predecessor's choices, kept): motion blur off (all motion < 4 mm/f); the tile floor has a faint self-emission ambient lift; the fill light is light-linked away from the pool; final 80 spp with MNEE caustics.
t_jelly_cubes: the 'one bold hero' is a trio of cubes, as the spec's 'three jelly cubes' requires.
open_issues: t_toy_town: around noon (about f75-f110) the shadows are short and fall behind the houses, out of the elevated camera's view. The light keeps changing (colour, brightness, faint shadow motion), but this is the calmest stretch of the tile.
t_jelly_cubes: the soft coloured glow-shadow of the airborne orange cube (f46-f60) brushes the lower-left hex corner, so a little soft shadow is cropped there. Nothing important is outside the hex.

t_sunset_bunny: mid-loop (about f61-f121) the bunny's shadow falls mostly behind it. The rotation then reads through the moving glints and reflections, and the gold reads amber-orange under the sunset light.
Costs were measured on an idle GPU 6, which is shared with other builders. Finals-queue wall time will be longer when the GPU is shared, but the GPU-h numbers are the idle measurements.
Full previews and finals were not rendered (per brief). The finals queue renders all frames.
notes_for_critic: Sheets: renders/review/t_*_sheet.png. Each has the hexagon outlined with the cropped corners dimmed. The stride rows come first, then a seam row (f loop+1 must equal f1), then a 1:1 row of 230x200 downscales for the 200 px check. Full-res frames are in renders/test/<id>/cost_v2 (bunny: cost_v3). Toy town is the new scene: look at f1 vs f180 for the shadow swing and at f150-f180 for the dusk window glow. Two roof decisions are deliberate: 45 and 54 deg glossy gables mirrored the noon sun into the camera and flared the hero's pink roof white, so the roofs are 40 deg satin candy. Bunny: compare renders/test/t_sunset_bunny/tint_off vs tint_a for the olive-patch fix. Duck: the bright specks are sun glints on ripple crests, not fireflies.
